newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China buys first diesel cargo after Lunar New Year.
newsitem.headline: China buys first diesel cargo after Lunar New Year.

text.p: China has bought its first gas oil (diesel) cargo since returning from the Lunar New Year break, paying $202 per tonne early this week, traders said on Thursday.
The 30,000-to-35,000-tonne cargo of 0.5-percent sulphur gas oil was sold by a major for end-February/early March delivery on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) southern China basis, they said.
The major also sold a 20,000-tonne parcel of gas oil this week for delivery to Hong Kong in early March at a premium of $1.10 per barrel to Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f.
Just before the holidays, China bought gas oil at $200 a tonne, c-and-f, with prices slipping briefly to below $200.
Sellers were now seeking around $204-$205 a tonne, c-and-f, based on current fob Singapore sale value of around $25.90 a barrel.
Traders said China was still expecting to buy more volumes if prices dipped to $200, c-and-f, or when fob Singapore values dropped to $25.30 a barrel.
Sellers said that at current levels, c-and-f Hong Kong prices should be around $1.20 per barrel above Singapore spot quotes.
China virtually disappeared from the gas oil market from mid-January and this largely contributed to the slump in regional prices from more than $32.00 barrel fob to around $25.00.
In December, when China bought more than 800,000 tonnes of gas oil, prices surged to $263 a tonne, c-and-f southern China.
Chinese sources said China was expected to take about 400,000-500,000 tonnes of gas oil in March.

With South Korea increasingly becoming a major regional gas oil supplier, with at least five cargoes available for export per month, China is expected to cover a large part of its requirements from Korea, traders said.
Before the Lunar New Year break, China bought gas oil from a South Korean refiner at a 10-cent-per-barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes, fob.
